The New Orleans Saints. A professional football franchise competing in the NFL's NFC South, founded in 1967 and based in New Orleans, Louisiana.

The team transformed from decades of mediocrity into a championship contender following the arrival of quarterback Drew Brees in 2006, coinciding with the city's recovery from Hurricane Katrina. That partnership produced the franchise's sole Super Bowl victory in Super Bowl 44 in February 2010 and created a powerful symbol of resilience and community redemption in American sports.

Founded in 1967, the franchise endured 39 years of losing records and futility before Drew Brees arrived, establishing themselves as an NFL perennial embarrassment. Drew Brees arrived in 2006 during the Saints' post-Katrina rebuilding phase, signing a contract to lead the franchise's resurrection just as New Orleans itself sought recovery.

The team won Super Bowl 44 in February 2010, the 2009 season, defeating the Indianapolis Colts and giving New Orleans its first championship, creating a transformative moment for the city's morale and identity. Head coach Sean Payton orchestrated the championship alongside Brees, employing innovative defensive schemes, the Blitzkrieg defense, and Brees's passing excellence to dominate opponents.

Drew Brees set numerous NFL passing records during his tenure from 2006 to 2019, becoming the franchise's most successful and celebrated player and revitalizing a dormant organization. The team remained competitive through the twenty-tens, winning multiple playoff appearances and division titles, though the post-Brees era beginning in 2020 has seen a return to inconsistency.

The 2009 championship became symbolic of New Orleans' resilience after Hurricane Katrina, with the Saints' victory serving as an emotional and cultural counterpoint to the devastation the city had endured just four years prior.
